# New flag is more noticeable (AH-0MVCFH6I4000AWRI)

## Problem statement

On the hold-full ("HULL FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP") reward overlay the `★ New`
marker for an item the player does not yet own is rendered as a small (14 px),
muted-orange detail line **beneath** the option's description, where it reads as
just another piece of detail copy. With three options on screen, a reduced-volume
ghost fire running and a 3-2-1 countdown competing for attention, players miss the
marker and read a brand-new item as an upgrade to something they already own.

## Users

- **Player (at-a-glance scan):** "As a player whose hold has just filled, I want
  brand-new offers to jump out of the list immediately, so I can tell 'this is
  something I don't own yet' from 'this is an upgrade' without reading every
  line."
- **Player (reward readability):** "As a player I want the New marker attached to
  the item's title so I cannot lose it in the description/countdown noise."
- **Designer / tuner:** "As a designer I want the emphasis produced by a single
  shared overlay implementation, so the game and every gym show the same
  presentation and the tuning lives in one place."

## Current behaviour (existing state)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` renders each option as a three-line block:
  1. title line `${index + 1}.  ${option.name}` — 20 px, cyan `#00ffff`,
     centred at `GAME_WIDTH / 2`, with `#111111` background padding;
  2. description line (13 px, `#cccccc`) at `y + 28`;
  3. detail line (14 px) at `y + 48` — the change summary
     (e.g. `+1 Projectiles`) or the string `★ New` in orange `#ff8800`
     (`CHOICE_NEW_COLOR`). `New` takes display priority over a change summary.
- The badge is static: no weight, no motion, no glow. Its container
  `getDetailLines()` is what the scene tests assert against.
- Existing agreed behaviour: **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4** specifies the badge as
  "a second, smaller detail line beneath the option name" and the three-line
  block is documented in the Game Design Document §4.5 and the README module
  entry for the overlay. Those two statements are what this item deliberately
  revises.
- Existing tests that pin the current presentation:
  `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` —
  `renders a "New" badge for options marked isNew` (asserts
  `getDetailLines()[0] === '★ New'`), `"New" badge takes display priority over
  changeSummary`, and `AC2 — shows a New option's description above its ★ New
  badge`.

## Desired change

1. Move the `★ New` marker to the **start of the title line**, ahead of the
   numbered name, so it is visually part of the item's heading.
2. Make it **bolder**: bold weight, larger than the current 14 px detail text,
   high-contrast treatment (stroke and/or text shadow) so it reads from a
   distance.
3. Give it **motion and light**: a continuous pulse (scale/alpha) plus a visible
   glow that intensifies with the pulse.
4. Stop repeating the marker on the detail line — the detail line keeps only the
   change summary (see Q2 below; the draft assumes removal).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Badge leads the title line.** For every option with `isNew`, the
  presetation renders the `★ New` marker on the **same row as the option title
  and to the left of that title** (reading order `★ New` → `1.` → item name), on
  the title line's vertical centre. Options without `isNew` render no marker.
- **AC2 — Bolder than before.** The marker is rendered in a bold weight with a
  font size strictly larger than the previous 14 px detail text, plus a visible
  stroke or text shadow, at a contrast that is at least as strong as the current
  `#ff8800` orange against the `#000000` backdrop.
- **AC3 — Pulses.** The marker animates continuously while the overlay is open
  with a yoyo tween over bounded properties (scale and/or alpha), period within
  600–1200 ms, scale amplitude ≤ 1.15 and alpha floor ≥ 0.6, so it stays inside
  its row (row pitch is 84 px) and never touches the title text or the
  neighbouring rows.
- **AC4 — Glows.** A visible glow accompanies the pulse (text shadow with blur
  and/or stroke) whose intensity is animated in step with AC3, remaining legible
  at every phase of the pulse.
- **AC5 — No duplicate marker, no layout regression.** The detail line no longer
  contains `★ New` (producer Q2 = A, revising AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4); change
  summaries continue to render beneath the description;
  `getOptionLabels()` still contains the option number and name; the existing
  three-line block (title → description → detail) and row pitch are preserved.
- **AC6 — Clean teardown.** Every pulse/glow tween is stopped and the marker
  objects destroyed when the selection countdown starts
  (`AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ` teardown path) and when the scene shuts down — no
  orphaned tweens or tweens targeting destroyed text.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The change lives once in the shared overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), so `PlayScene` and every gym that opens it present the
  identical marker; no divergent copy is introduced.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Scene tests cover: marker present at the title
  line start for `isNew` options and absent otherwise; bold/larger style
  asserted; pulse tween exists with the expected target properties and is
  removed on teardown; detail line no longer carries `★ New` while change
  summaries still render. Each test asserts a behaviour, not internal constants.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** Game Design Document §4.5 and the README
  `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` entry describe the title-line marker with
  its pulse/glow, and the code comments in the scene are updated. (CHANGELOG is
  handled by the release pipeline and is out of scope.)
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Single shared implementation.** `MineralChoiceScene` is consumed by
  `PlayScene` and every gym (`GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, …); the
  marker is implemented once there. No per-launcher option or flag.
- **Phaser 4 text only.** No new sprites or binary assets; the glow is achieved
  with Phaser text styling (`stroke`, `shadow`) and tweens.
- **Demo/attract mode safe.** The demo launcher auto-selects after a delay
  (`autoSelectMs`). The pulse must not delay, block or interfere with selection,
  the 3-2-1 countdown, or the ghost-fire metronome.
- **No new settings surface.** There is no reduced-motion setting in
  `configStore` today; this item does not add one (bounded amplitude keeps the
  motion mild). If the producer wants a visibility/reduce-motion toggle, that is
  a separate item.
- **Headless eval unaffected.** The perception-free eval arena never opens the
  overlay, so no eval-parity work is required; the existing parity tests keep
  guarding shared behaviour.

## Existing state / Desired change summary

| Aspect | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| Position | detail line under the description (`y + 48`) | start of the title line, left of `1.  <name>` |
| Weight | regular 14 px | bold, larger than 14 px, stroked/shadowed |
| Motion | none | continuous bounded pulse + glow |
| Detail line | `★ New` or change summary | change summary only |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — add the title-line marker text object,
  style constants (size/colour/stroke/shadow), pulse/glow tween creation and
  teardown, plus a test accessor (e.g. `getNewBadges()` returning the marker
  texts/tweens) alongside the existing `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()`
  accessors.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — revise the three existing
  `New` badge assertions to the new contract and add placement, style, tween and
  teardown coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full choice overlay bullet: marker
  presentation (title-line start, bold, pulsing, glowing).
- `README.md` — `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` module entry: same
  description in the three-line block summary.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** (completed) — introduced the change summary and the
  `★ New` badge as a detail line; AC4 is the statement this item revises.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** (completed) — added the description line and the
  three-line block that positions the marker today.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** (completed) — created the shared hold-full overlay and
  its zero-launcher-knowledge contract.
- **AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ** (completed) — countdown + teardown path the pulse must
  respect.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** (completed) — power-up levelling, which made the badge
  apply to power-ups as well as weapons (so up to three markers can be on screen
  at once).
- **AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z** (completed) — sibling hold-full-screen item, same area
  of the overlay (recent precedent for intake → implement on this screen).

## Assumptions (A1–A2 confirmed by the producer; A3–A5 are implementation defaults)

- **A1.** The marker text stays `★ New` (uppercase-initial, star prefix) rather
  than becoming `NEW` / `NEW!`; only its weight, size, position, motion and glow
  change. Rationale: it keeps the wording players have seen and keeps the
  existing string assertions meaningful.
- **A2.** The base colour stays the orange `CHOICE_NEW_COLOR` (`#ff8800`); the
  glow adds light (white/amber shadow) rather than changing the hue.
- **A3.** The pulse runs continuously for as long as the overlay is open (one
  tween per marker), rather than pulsing a fixed number of times.
- **A4.** Marker motion is implemented per-marker with the same tween
  configuration; no per-index phase offset (three markers pulsing in step is
  acceptable).
- **A5.** The marker does not change the overlay's width, centring rules or the
  row pitch; the title line is laid out as `[marker][gap][numbered name]` with
  both anchored relative to the existing centred title.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> Recorded via `/skill:intake`. All three interview questions were answered by
> the producer (2026-10-25, interactive reply), each with the recommended option
> **A**; no open questions remain.

- **Q1 — Does the marker become a separate object beside the title, or become
  part of the title string?**
  Options: **(A)** a separate text object anchored to the left of the existing

# UFO Feel — Intake brief (final, producer answers incorporated)

**FINAL DRAFT** — producer answered Q1=B, Q2=C, Q3=A (see Appendix).
Stage to follow: intake_complete (via intake finish + coverage review).

## Problem statement

The Mystery UFO collector drone flies, harvests and dies **silently and
without feedback**: it has no visual effects and no sounds for any lifecycle
moment, so the reward reads as dead game feel. We need the classic Space
Invaders mystery-ship juice: a "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble while it is deployed,
a reward cue when it returns to the player, and an explosion plus a "tinkle" of
dropped resources when it is destroyed — with full-juice VFX at every lifecycle
stage.

## Users

- **Player** (the primary stakeholder) — wants the Mystery UFO to *feel* like
  the Space Invaders homage it is: an audible, celebratory arcade reward with
  visible juice at spawn, on collect, on return and on death.
- **Developer / quality gates** — wants the juice to run through the existing
  ToneForge audio pipeline and shared VFX so the game and every gym stay
  identical (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole
  sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.
- As a player, I want to see the saucer come alive (running-light pulse, a poof
  on launch, sparkles as it vacuums, a trail on the way home) so the drone
  reads as a living reward.
- As a player, I want a reward fanfare when the drone flies home and pays out
  so the economic payoff feels earned.
- As a player, I want a satisfying explosion and the tinkle of minerals
  scattering when an enemy shoots the drone down, so the loss/opportunity
  reads clearly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Warble loop (Q2=C).** A classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays
   continuously from spawn through the **seek and collect** phases (the whole
   sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is
   destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with
   control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a
   level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute
   settings.
2. **Reward cue (Q3=A).** A distinct reward fanfare plays on **arrival at the
   player**, synchronised with the hold pay-in (exactly when
   `MysteryUfoDrone._payOut` credits the sink), so the payout moment is
   audible.
3. **Destruction feedback.** On enemy destruction the drone plays an explosion
   cue **and** spawns the explosion particle VFX at the crash site (reusing
   `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`); a mineral "tinkle" cue fires in sync with
   the spilled resource drops (spill already exists via
   `hitDrone`/`scatterMineralDrops`), so the dropped minerals read audibly.
4. **Full-juice VFX (Q1=B).** Code-drawn Phaser graphics (no external art) add
   the full lifecycle juice: spawn poof at launch, per-mineral collect
   sparkle/ring while vacuuming, a running-light pulse animation on the saucer
   rim, and a return-leg trail/glow — all in addition to the destruction
   explosion VFX.
5. **Pipeline, parity & quality.** Every new cue is a baked ToneForge delivery
   (recipe YAMLs under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, entries in
   `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, wrappers in `src/audio/effects.ts`, WAVs
   rendered via `npm run build-audio`); the cue-manifest / effects-contract /
   build-audio / audio-balance-guard suites pass; the continuous warble has
   start/stop control lifecycle and every cue degrades to a safe no-op without
   an AudioContext; the VFX/SFX run through shared core so `PlayScene` and the
   gym scenes are identical (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion
   pass, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` green); the full project test suite
   passes and relevant docs (GDD §7.3 / Mystery UFO section,
   `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`) are updated.

## Constraints

- Audio must flow through the existing ToneForge pipeline — no new external
  assets (procedural WAV baked at build time; `file:../ToneForge` dependency).
- The continuous warble requires start/stop control lifecycle (`ControlCues` in
  the manifest) and must respect the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
- VFX must be code-drawn Phaser graphics (repo convention: no external art).
- Every cue must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests and
  autoplay-blocked browsers) — the effects contract suite enforces this.
- Behaviour must live once in shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and be consumed
  by both the game and the gyms (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- Peak-volume/balance guarded by `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs`.

## Existing state

- `MysteryUfoDrone` (src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts) is a pure entity with a
  code-drawn saucer (running lights, dome, glow) but **zero VFX/SFX**: no cue is
  called anywhere in the drone, the shared pass (`src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`),
  or the spawn path. Collection (`_vacuum`) hides minerals with no feedback;
  destruction (`_destroyByEnemy` + `hitDrone`) already spills minerals via
  `scatterMineralDrops` but with no explosion/tinkle feedback.
- The audio pipeline is ToneForge-baked: `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps
  every cue to a recipe; `src/audio/effects.ts` exports thin playback wrappers;
  WAVs are baked by `npm run build-audio`. No UFO cue exists yet.

## Desired change

Add the "feel" layer so every Mystery UFO lifecycle moment gives feedback
through the shared pipeline, identically in the game and the gyms: warble for
the whole sortie, a reward fanfare on payout, explosion + mineral tinkle +
particle burst on destruction, plus the full-juice VFX set (spawn poof, collect
sparkle, running-light pulse, return trail).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — lifecycle state hooks (spawn, collect,
  return, payout, destroyed) driving the SFX/VFX seams; running-light pulse
  animation in the saucer draw/update.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` — shared tick/spawn/destroy pass: warble
  start/stop in `tickDrones`, destruction explosion + tinkle adjacent to the
  existing spill in `hitDrone`, spawn poof in `spawnDrone`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` /
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shared wiring so game and gyms run the same code.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue wrappers: warble loop + `stopMysteryUfoWarbleSound`
  control companion, `playMysteryUfoRewardSound`, `playMysteryUfoDestroySound`,
  `playMineralTinkleSound`.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue→recipe entries (+ control cue).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — new `aihell-mystery-ufo-*` recipes
  (warble, reward, destroy, mineral tinkle).
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` / `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`
  — continuous-cue start/stop plumbing for the warble.
- `src/vfx/` — spawn poof, collect sparkle/ring, return trail (small new/module
  effects, following `explosionParticles.ts` conventions); `explosionParticles.ts`
  reused for the destruction burst.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§7.3 + Mystery UFO section),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G113S009B37I** — Mystery UFO has no visible representation (epic,
  completed): the collector-drone entity and shared pass this item adds feel to.
- **AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92** — Mystery UFO needs a better graphical representation
  (completed): the code-drawn saucer VFX baseline this item animates.
- **AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7** — Space Invaders mystery UFO bonus (completed): the
  classic reference the warble/reward homage draws from.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J** — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge (epic): the pipeline every new cue must flow through.
- **AH-0MVBMPZ2C0008VAE** — Drone level variables and curve specs (completed).
- **AH-0MVBMQ0HR0064THH** — Gym parity for the collector drone (completed).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **VFX scope.** "The item says the Mystery UFO currently has no VFX or
  SFX but does not specify which visual effects to add. (a) Minimal...; (b)
  Full juice — also add spawn poof, return-trail/glow, running-light pulse;
  (c) Sound-only."
  — Answer (producer, via review reply "1. B (with SFX)"): **B — full juice**,
  with the SFX set confirmed in scope alongside the VFX. Source: producer
  review reply on AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6 (comment thread
  AH-C0MVNZ64M5000W4NL). Final AC 4 (full-juice VFX) + ACs 1–3 (SFX) reflect
  this.
- Q2: **"woo-woo-woo" delivery.** "(a) continuous looping cue while the drone
  is in the collect phase; (b) discrete one-shot per collected mineral; (c) a
  looping cue that plays for the whole sortie (seek+collect)."
  — Answer (producer, "2. C"): **C — loop for the whole sortie** (seek +
  collect), so the warble starts at spawn and ends at return/payout/destruction.
  Source: producer review reply. Final AC 1 reflects this.
- Q3: **Reward timing.** "(a) on arrival at the ship, synchronised with the
  payout pay-in; (b) when the drone begins the return leg; (c) both."
  — Answer (producer, "3. A"): **A — on arrival/payout**, synced with the hold
  credit. Source: producer review reply. Final AC 2 reflects this.

### Assumptions (documented)

- The original description's "no VFX or VFX" is a typo for "no VFX or SFX"
  (confirmed implicitly by Q1 answer B *with SFX*).
- Level progression (lifetime/capacity/radius) does **not** change the sound
  character — same cues at every level (no per-level variant recipes).
- New cues respect the existing volume balance budget (≤ ~0.2 peak per layer,
  `audio-balance-guard`) and the global SFX mute/volume settings automatically
  via the shared playback provider.
- Running-light pulse is a static-free animation of the existing
  code-drawn lights (alpha/colour oscillation), not a new emitter.

### Risks

- **Audio-pipeline risk (med).** Every new cue is a build-time WAV bake: recipe
  YAML, manifest entry, wrapper and `npm run build-audio` render must stay in
  lock-step or the contract suites (cue-manifest / effects-contract /
  build-audio / audio-balance-guard) fail red. Mitigation: follow the exact
  pattern of an existing baked cue (e.g. `aihell-diver-dive-loop`) end to end.
- **Continuous-cue lifecycle risk (med).** The sortie-long warble must start
  exactly once at spawn and stop on every terminal path (return, payout,
  destroyed, teardown) or it will leak a looping voice. Mitigation: start/stop
  via the shared control-companion pattern (`ControlCues`) and asset in
  `tickDrones` where removal is final; extend the cue-contract test to assert
  stop-on-all-terminals.
- **Collect-sparkle VFX performance (low-med).** At the max collector radius
  (40 px) a drone can vacuum several minerals in one tick; a sparkle per
  mineral must be small, short-lived and capped, not an unbounded emitter.
  Mitigation: reuse `explosionParticles`-style pooled graphics and cap per-tick
  spawns.
- **Parity risk (med).** If a gym or `PlayScene` wires the SFX/VFX outside the
  shared core, the duplicate-body guard / gym-parity docs assertion fail and
  the game and gyms drift. Mitigation: implement through
  `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` and shared hooks only (AGENTS.md
  architecture convention).
- **Scope-creep risk (med).** The chosen full-juice VFX set (poof, sparkle,
  pulse, trail) is wide for one item. Extra polish discovered during
  implementation (e.g. pay-in burst on the ship, level-scaled bloom) must be
  recorded as new work items, not absorbed into this one.

### Duplicate-work check

Performed `wl search "UFO"` / `"woo"` / `"mystery ufo vfx"` — completed items
cover visual representation (AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92), visibility epic
(AH-0MV9G113S009B37I) and the classic reference (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7); **no
overlapping item for UFO audio/VFX feel exists**. No duplicate — proceed.

# Salvage has no visible effect (AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09)

## Problem statement

While the **Salvage** bounty window is active, each destroyed non-hazard enemy
drops the level-resolved bonus minerals at the wreck, but those minerals render
as exactly the same gold dots as every ordinary mineral. The bounty therefore
has no *visible* effect: the player cannot tell whether the extra minerals came
from Salvage, and the pickup feels inert even though the mechanic is wired.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (bounty chooser):** *As a player who collected or chose Salvage, when
  I destroy an enemy I want the bonus minerals to look different from ordinary
  minerals, so I can see the bounty paying out and judge whether it was worth
  the pickup.*
- **Player (economy reading):** *As a player reading the mineral field, I want
  ordinary mineral drops to stay gold, so the baseline economy stays readable
  and the orange dots uniquely mean "Salvage bonus".*

## Current behaviour (verified in the repo)

- `EffectsRegistry.salvageBonusMinerals()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns
  `0` unless the timed window is active, otherwise the level-resolved
  `salvageMinerals` (curve base **1** → cap **4**, k=0.35).
- The shared kill seam adds exactly that many extra minerals at the wreck
  through `scatterMineralDrops(...)`:
  - `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, in the kill handler, just after
    `resolveMineralKillDrops`);
  - `GymFormationScene._dropMineralsForKill`
    (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
  Both guard with `isNonBlockingHazard(...)` / the `getSizeTier` test, so
  **asteroids and lane hazards are excluded** — Salvage pays out for destroyed
  **ships** only, even though the original report assumed "ships and/or
  asteroids".
- The HUD already lists a Salvage row while the window is active
  (`src/ui/HUD.ts`, `case 'salvage'` → `reg.isActive(id)`), so a countdown
  readout exists. The visibility gap is purely the **drop rendering**.
- `Mineral` hard-codes `MINERAL_COLOR` (`0xffdd44`, gold) in `_drawBody()`
  (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), and `scatterMineralDrops` accepts no colour, so
  every mineral in the game and in every gym is visually identical.

## Desired change

Give **Salvage bonus minerals their own colour — orange** — while every other
mineral stays gold, in the game and in every gym, through one shared code path.
The change is cosmetic: an orange salvage mineral is still worth exactly one
mineral.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Orange salvage drops.** While the Salvage window is active, the bonus
   minerals spawned at a destroyed enemy's wreck render **orange**, and every
   other mineral (asteroid drop, enemy re-drop, seeded gym field, drone spill)
   continues to render **gold**. Covered by unit tests in the game
   (`PlayScene`) and in the formation gym (`GymFormationScene`).
2. **Single source of colour.** The orange is defined once as a named constant
   (`MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR`) beside `MINERAL_COLOR` in `src/core/constants.ts`;
   `Mineral` accepts an optional colour (default `MINERAL_COLOR`), so all
   existing callers keep the gold default unchanged.
3. **One shared seam (gym↔game parity).** Game and gyms spawn salvage drops
   through **one** shared helper (e.g. `scatterSalvageMineralDrops` next to
   `scatterMineralDrops`), and the repo-wide defined-once guard in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` covers it, so the colour
   and scatter maths cannot drift between `PlayScene` and the gyms.
4. **No behaviour, economy or RNG change.** Each salvage mineral is still worth
   one mineral, the bonus count still comes from
   `salvageBonusMinerals()`, asteroids remain excluded, and the scatter helper
   consumes the same two RNG draws per drop in the same order (existing
   determinism/draw-order tests stay green).
5. **Visible in a real run.** With Salvage active, an enemy kill leaves orange
   dots on the field next to any gold drops, so the effect is legible to the
   player without reading the HUD.
6. **Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4 Salvage entry / §4.4.1 minerals
   "Dropping" bullet), `README.md`'s mineral section and the relevant code
   comments all describe the orange salvage drop.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Cosmetic only: no new drop type, no value change, no magnet/scoop behaviour
  change, no HUD redesign.
- Keep the existing `scatterMineralDrops` signature backwards compatible
  (optional colour parameter or an additive helper), so the many current
  callers (asteroid drops, enemy re-drops, collector-drone spill, gym seeding)
  are untouched.
- The orange must be clearly distinct from gold and from existing gameplay
  colours (enemy fire reds/pinks, power-up bubble colours); confirm the chosen
  value against the bullet/pickup palettes before picking it.
- No new procedural timers or per-frame work — this is a fill colour at spawn.

## Existing state

- Salvage is already fully wired (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`): bonus minerals spawn
  through the shared kill seam in `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, and the
  integration test `AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Salvage adds bonus minerals at a
  destroyed enemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) proves the count grows.
- The only missing piece is a distinguishable render colour for those drops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR` (orange) with a doc
  comment next to `MINERAL_COLOR`.
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — optional `color` on `MineralConfig`, `_drawBody()`
  uses `config.color ?? MINERAL_COLOR`, plus an optional colour argument (or
  additive helper) on the scatter function.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared re-export / seam for the
  salvage-coloured scatter helper so both scenes import one thing.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — use the shared salvage-drop helper.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — use the same shared salvage-drop
  helper (parity).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend the defined-once
  guard to the new helper.
- Tests: `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (or
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`), a
  `GymFormationScene` salvage-colour test, and
  `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` if the seam lives there.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 Salvage entry and the §4.4.1
  minerals "Dropping" bullet) and `README.md` (minerals section).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed):** wired
  `salvageBonusMinerals()` into the shared kill seam (game + gyms). This item is
  the visual follow-up to that wiring.
- **AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 — 5 net-new power-ups (completed):** introduced the
  Salvage catalogue entry, its level curves (1 → 4 bonus minerals, 10 → 20 s)
  and the HUD readout.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold (completed):** owns the `Mineral` entity, `MINERAL_COLOR` and the
  shared scatter maths this change extends.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Document gym-parity principle (completed):** the rule
  that an enabled behaviour runs the same code in the game and every gym; this
  brief therefore demands one shared salvage-drop helper.
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S — Asteroids drop more lives (completed):** precedent for
  a kill-drop variant added to the same shared kill seam.
- Repo/docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (Salvage) and §4.4.1
  (Minerals, the Ship's Hold & the Power-Up Choice); `README.md` minerals
  section; `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` (shared kill-drop rule).

### Automated find-related report

- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** – Power ups need to be larger (completed)
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S** – Asteroids drop more lives (completed)
- **AH-0MU8FOQM0007D94Z** – Enemy Config + Factory Wiring + Unit Tests (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Out of scope (follow-up candidates, not this item)

- Adding a HUD "Salvage +N" bonus suffix or a pickup flourish. If the colour
  alone proves insufficient, raise a `discovered-from:AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09`
  item rather than widening this one.
- Making Salvage apply to asteroids/hazards (it deliberately does not).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a distinct colour is enough to make the bounty legible.
  Justification: the complaint is that the extra drops are indistinguishable;
  the HUD already exposes the active window and its bonus level.
- **Risk (visual collision):** orange may read like enemy fire or a hazard.
  Mitigation: pick a hue/saturation clearly outside the enemy-bullet palette,
  keep the small-dot silhouette, and note the choice in the constant's comment.
- **Risk (parity drift):** if `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each passed a
  colour literal they could diverge. Mitigation: one shared helper + the
  defined-once equivalence guard.
- **Risk (RNG determinism):** touching the scatter helper could reorder draws.
  Mitigation: additive/optional parameter only; existing draw-order tests must
  stay green.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "while I am here" ideas (new mineral tiers, value
  changes, HUD redesign) are recorded above as out of scope, not folded in.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **No clarifying questions were needed.** The seed context ("make the extra
  items dropped a different colour, perhaps orange") already fixes the desired
  outcome. Research resolved the remaining unknowns from the repo:
  - Salvage applies to destroyed **ships only**, not asteroids — the kill seams
    exclude non-blocking hazards (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`).
  - The extra drops are already spawned (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`), so this is a
    rendering-only change.
  - The HUD already shows the active Salvage row, so no HUD work is required.
- **Assumptions recorded as resolved decisions:** orange = the salvage colour;
  everything else stays gold; the change is cosmetic (1 mineral per dot); the
  colour is exposed as a constant plus an optional `Mineral` config field.

# Intake Brief — AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in mini-boss reward screen (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F)

## Problem statement

*"When the AI beats the mini boss it should be able to select an item from the
reward screen and carry on."* (original seed description)

When the demo/attract-mode bot defeats a mini-boss, `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward()`
opens the shared `MineralChoiceScene` overlay **without** the demo-only auto-select
parameters (`autoSelectMs` / `autoSelectIndex`) that the hold-full choice path
(`openMineralChoice`) passes. The overlay therefore waits forever for a human
selection, so the bot-driven demo run **stalls** on the mini-boss reward screen
instead of picking an upgrade/unlock and carrying on.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** — *"As a viewer of the arcade-attract demo, I want the

# Enemy force fields scale with level progression

**Headline:** Add data-driven enemy force fields that appear from a per-archetype
start level (some enemies shielded from level 2, others later) and grow stronger
with each level, absorbing a number of player hits before the ship inside is
exposed and destroyed as normal.

## Problem statement

Deeper campaign levels currently raise threat only through raw enemy density and
firepower; each regular enemy is still a single-hit (or fixed 5-hit) target. The
result is that upgraded weapons trivialise late-level fodder. Adding a
**force-field layer** — a distinct, readable barrier that absorbs several hits
before the ship inside becomes vulnerable — gives the late campaign a new
escalation axis that existing durability (`EnemyConfig.health`) does not provide,
without touching weapon/power-up economies.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want enemies in deeper levels to absorb a few hits behind a
  visible barrier, so late-game firepower is challenged again and reading a
  shielded enemy (barrier first, hull second) is intuitive.
- **As a balance engineer**, I want force-field strength (which archetypes are
  shielded, from which level, and how the field's hit count grows) to be
  data-driven and tunable per enemy, so I can shape difficulty without scene
  code.
- **As a developer**, I want the force-field logic to live once in the shared
  core so the game and every gym behave identically, with no divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven per-archetype fields.** New `EnemyConfig` fields
  `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which this archetype first gains a
  field; `0` = never shielded), `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it
  appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits` (field hits at the campaign maximum level)
  are added to the CSV schema/codec, config types and seed defaults, each
  defaulting so that **every existing enemy is unshielded at level 1** and the
  shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged until at least level 2. Field
  strength at any level is `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @
  10)), 0, 5)` via a pure, Phaser-free shared resolver. Heavier archetypes
  (Tank/Harvester) carry higher base values than light ones.
- **AC2 — Force-field absorbs hits before the hull.** A shielded enemy survives
  its fleet of field hits first; each absorbed hit consumes the bullet (with
  feedback) but does **not** decrement `EnemyConfig.health`. Only after the
  field is broken does the enemy's normal health apply (so most archetypes die
  on the next hit; the 5-HP Harvester still needs 5). Every player damage source
  (normal bullet, piercing, AOE weapons, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy
  bonus hits) depletes the field through the existing shared `takeDamage()`
  seam — no parallel damage path. Player contact/ram: a shielded enemy's field
  absorbs the ram — exactly one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives, the
  player survives the collision and is not destroyed. Once the field is down,
  the existing contact rule applies unchanged (both destroyed,
  AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). The absorb must be one field hit per ram contact, not
  per overlapping frame (documented re-arm, mirroring the Thorn Field ram
  absorption in `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4).
- **AC3 — Readable feedback.** Shielded enemies render a shared bubble drawn by
  the `CombatEffectVisuals` helper family, visually distinct from the player's
  Shield and Force Field bubbles; each absorbed hit triggers the existing shared
  impact feedback; the breaking hit runs a distinct break flash/audio cue.
- **AC4 — Gym parity and tunability.** The same resolver drives the game
  (`PlayScene` spawn path, run level from `WaveManager`) and the level gym
  (`GymLevel`), with a parity test. The enemy-config gym editor
  (`GymFodderEnemies` slider surface) gains force-field controls so a
  formation-gym (no campaign context) spawn can force a field on with a given
  hit count; the divergence (gym slider sets hits directly instead of a level
  curve) is recorded in the code and this item.
- **AC5 — Verification and documentation.** Unit tests cover the resolver curve
  (start level, ramp, clamping, cap, L1-unchanged), CSV codec defaults, entity
  absorb/break behaviour, and scene integration; game↔gym parity test passes;
  the duplicate-body guard stays green; a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10
  records `survivalSeconds`, `levelReached`, `avoidableHits` and
  `enemiesKilledByArchetype` before/after (or demonstrates the field keeps the
  campaign playable). GDD §2.6 (remove "no shield layer"), §4.1 and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` are updated with the new behaviour
  and tuning table; **all related documentation is updated** and the **full
  project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (repo `AGENTS.md`): enabled gameplay
  behaviour is shared code consumed by the game and every relevant gym; only a
  documented disabled feature may diverge. The force-field resolver and bubble
  helper must live in the shared core, not per-scene copies.
- **Level 1 is untouched.** Defaults guarantee zero shielded enemies at level 1,
  preserving onboarding, tests and the existing balance baseline.
- **No changes to enemy `health`, weapon/power-up economies, or the player
  Force Field / Shield power-ups.** Fields are a new, additive layer.
- **Backwards-compatible config persistence** — existing enemy config blobs and
  the CSV load with the new fields defaulted (`0`); no schema break.
- **Determinism** — field strength is a pure function of (level, config); same
  level + seed ⇒ identical shields, so the fixed/curve campaign determinism
  contract is preserved.
- **No new player-facing UI** beyond the in-game bubble and gym editor controls.

## Existing state

- Regular-enemy health is data-driven (`EnemyConfig.health`, default 1; Harvester
  5 HP) and applied via `BaseEnemy.takeDamage()` — the shared damage seam every
  damage source already routes through (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`:
  bullet, piercing, AOE, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy).
- `EnemyConfig` is CSV-backed (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with a numeric
  codec (`src/core/csv.ts`), seed defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) and a
  **gym enemy editor** slider surface (`GymFodderEnemies.ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`).
- Spawn seam: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` → `loadEnemyConfig(key)` →
  `createEnemyFromConfig`; the run level is available via `WaveManager.level`.
  `GymLevel` launches real campaign waves through the same factory.
- The **player** has Shield (absorbs hits) and Gradius-style Force Field
  (reflects bullets) power-ups; neither has any enemy-side counterpart. GDD
  §2.6 currently states "no shield layer", which this feature deliberately
  changes.
- Level-scaling work is in flight (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): its contract tests
  (AH-0MVLJCYGW001TRB3) are done; the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` implementation
  (`AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X`) is pending.

## Desired change

1. Add `forceFieldStartLevel` / `forceFieldStartHits` / `forceFieldMaxHits` to
   `EnemyConfig` (types, CSV codec, seed defaults, CSV rows; default 0/1/1).
2. Add a pure resolver (proposed `src/core/enemyForceField.ts`,
   `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)`); coordinate reuse of
   `levelScaling.ts` plumbing if F1 (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) has landed.
3. Thread the resolved field hits into entity spawn (game and level gym through
   the shared factory/config path) and implement field state + bubble in
   `BaseEnemy` (draw, absorb decrement, break effects); keep `takeDamage()`
   consuming the field before `health`. Add the **ram-absorb branch** to
   `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4 (one field hit per ram contact,
   player and enemy both survive; falls through to the existing both-destroyed
   rule once the field is down) — shared, so the game and every gym inherit it.
4. Add the shared bubble/break visuals to `CombatEffectVisuals` and any new SFX
   cue to the audio registry; add the gym-editor force-field sliders.
5. Tests: TDD contract tests for the resolver/codec/entity, game↔gym parity,
   and a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10.
6. Update GDD §2.6/§4.1 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; refresh
   the enemy-config CSV header comments.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — Add `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` + `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Seed defaults and per-archetype values (`0` default = never/unchanged).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — Numeric codec support for the new columns (default 0).
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **New** pure resolver `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` (curve, clamp, cap 5, L1 = 0).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Field state, bubble draw, absorb-before-health in `takeDamage()`, break feedback, ram-absorb entry point.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (+ `CombatScene.test.ts`) — Ram-absorb branch in `_handleCollisions` step 4 with the shared re-arm, mirroring `tryConsumeThornsRam`. Note: this file is **shared core**, so the change lands once for the game and all gyms.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread effective field hits into entity construction from config.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Resolve and pass field hits at spawn (run level via `WaveManager`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (+ `GymBotTuning`/`GymCurveSequencer` if they spawn campaign waves) — same resolver for parity.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — Force-field sliders/controls on the enemy-config editor (documented divergence: direct hits, no level curve).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (+ tests) — Shared enemy-force-field bubble + break flash helper.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Any field-break cue (reuse existing cues where possible).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Game↔gym parity block stays green.
- `src/core/*.test.ts`, `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts` — Resolver, codec, entity, integration tests.
- `src/ai/eval/` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Bot-batch evidence mode at L1/L5/L10 (extend the F5 per-level harness if landed).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Behaviour + tuning table.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P** (in-progress epic) — Level-scaled enemy counts / power-up drops; the level-scaling infrastructure (`levelScaling.ts`, F1 AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) that this feature coordinates with.
- **AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2** (completed) — Harvester + data-driven multi-hit `health`; the seam this feature extends.
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** (completed) — Shared multi-hit kill finalisation / `takeDamage` seam.
- **AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR** (completed) — Data-driven enemy health config (CSV codec + editor).
- **AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT** (completed) — Contact rule: player crashing into an enemy destroys both. **Extended by this item** (Q6 = B): a shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram (one field hit, both survive); unshielded enemies keep the original rule.
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** (open) — Player Force Field feedback (distinct scope; do not conflate).
- **AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S** (open) — Wave Laser limited hit power (piercing interplay; verify AOE/piercing behaviour against the field).
- Repo `AGENTS.md` — Gym↔game parity convention.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5** – Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules in GDD (Wall vs Dive Bomb) (completed)
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** – More forcefield feedback (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destroyed, enemies, exposed, fields, force (+13 more); the enemy-build/health seams this feature extends
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: the GDD §2.6/§4.1 floor the "no shield layer" rule this item changes
- `README.md` — matched: broad gameplay terms; check for any shield/level claims on release

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the three-field linear model (start level, start hits, max hits at L10) is the right "per-enemy curve variation" shape; operator confirmed per-enemy tunable start levels (some L2, others L3+) and "subtle variations of this curve for different enemies".
- **Assumption:** "killed in a single hit" after field break applies to the 1-HP majority; the Harvester keeps its 5 HP once its field is down (AC2, operator Q2 = A).
- **Assumption (confirmed, Q6 = B):** a shielded enemy's field also absorbs a player **contact/ram** — exactly one field hit is consumed and both sides survive the collision; the pre-existing rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies once the field is down.
- **Assumption (implementation detail, flagged):** "one field hit per ram" needs a re-arm so a sustained overlap cannot drain the whole field frame-by-frame. Proposed: a documented ram re-arm cooldown (~0.5 s) resolved once in the shared core; recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix for the review gate.
- **Risk:** force fields stack with the level-scaling density/drop changes (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and could push late levels into bullet-sink tedium; mitigated by the 5-hit cap, per-archetype defaults, and bot-batch survival evidence.
- **Risk:** heavy archetypes (Tank/Harvester) with fields at L2–3 may frustrate players who maxed weapons; mitigated by keeping light archetypes unshielded for longer and tuning via CSV.
- **Risk:** the gym slider for formation gyms bypasses the level curve, so an editor could author values the campaign never produces; documented divergence + editorial note in the gym panel.
- **Risk:** editing the CSV schema/editor touches shared tooling (codec, gym panel, docs tests); keep defaults `0` so existing rows and persisted blobs load unchanged.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no retuning of enemy health, weapon levels, drop rates or the player shield/force-field power-ups; separate items are created for any of those discovered during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers


- **Q6 — Should a shielded enemy absorb a player ram with its field, or is contact unchanged (both destroyed) as AC2 originally stated?** Options: (A) unchanged — ram destroys both regardless of field; (B) field absorbs the ram — one field hit is consumed and the player survives the collision; (C) field breaks entirely on ram, enemy survives, player destroyed. — **Answer (operator): B.** Source: interactive reply to the plan skill. A shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram: one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives and the player survives the collision. Once the field is down the original contact rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies. AC2 and the Risks section were rewritten accordingly. Precedent reused: Thorn Field's ram absorption (`tryConsumeThornsRam`) in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` step 4 of `_handleCollisions`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (Q6 follow-on, for the producer at the plan review gate):** how long is the ram re-arm after a field absorbs a ram? Without one, a held overlap consumes a field hit every frame and drains the field instantly. **Recommended:** a dedicated ~0.5 s shared re-arm constant (do *not* reuse the post-hit invulnerability window, which would also grant blink immunity). Directed to: Producer — affects feel and the field's effective durability against ramming.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.

- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).
